summary: Owner decision on #352 (2026-11-03): record In Metaph. IX, lect. 8 n. 11 ('quousque veniatur ad primum movens, quod est in actu tantum') as a stating claim for STMT-FIRST-UNMOVED-MOVER-IS-PURE-ACT, settling item (d) of ATTEMPT-LAMBDA7-FIRST-MOVER-PURE-ACT. Witness: the existing pinned passage AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-IX-L7-L9 (Corpus Thomisticum web snapshot), materialized; lect. 8 read whole, with lect. 7 n. 4-8 (priority in time, to which n. 11 refers back with 'ut supra dictum est'). Fidelity: 'in actu tantum' has no restricting phrase, unlike lect. 9 n. 6 ('inquantum huiusmodi', potency 'secundum quid'), so it is read as PureAct (no potency in any respect); the positive 'in act' is not formalized. 'Primum movens' (the end of the series of agents 'generans aut movens aut faciens', each requiring a prior act) is read as a first mover moved by none, on DISAMB-MOTION's broad reading; the definite singular is read as a universal, with no existence or uniqueness added. Limits: said in passing, without a reason for 'tantum'; the stated regress only reaches a first mover and does not exclude its dormant potency in a respect in which it does not move (the gap of ACT-PRIOR-FROM-INCORRUPTIBLE-FACTS). The claim is a stated commitment, not an argument. Rejected sibling: 'tantum' restricted to the act by which it moves; nothing in the sentence restricts it, and that content is already STMT-NOTHING-MOVES-EXCEPT-AS-IN-ACT. Frontier: --reaching-root unchanged (81 open: 29 bare, 52 sourced; same set). --routes: CATHOLICISM-SKELETON 31 to 29 (now cheapest), CATHOLICISM-FROM-PRIMA-VIA 36 to 35, -VIA-MAXIME-ENS 39 to 38; others unchanged. STMT-ACT-SIMPLY-PRIOR-TO-POTENCY still reaches the root through the stage-2 arguments.
